findings.title: Call to nonexistent zero-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled method prevents compilation
findings.body: UsernameForm calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but its superclass only declares `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` and neither this class nor AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator defines a zero-argument overload. This is a Java compile-time method resolution error, so the services module cannot be built until the call supplies a user or a matching overload is added.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys are disabled for all initial unauthenticated login forms
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` now requires `user != null`, while both `authenticate` and the error challenge use it to decide whether to call `fillContextForm`. During a normal initial login there is no context user, so the WebAuthn conditional-UI attributes and challenge are never populated. This removes passkey/autofill authentication from the initial UsernamePasswordForm flow (and from UsernameForm through the inherited authenticate path), contradicting the existing initial-login tests that expect the `webauth` form and preventing passkey-only users from signing in. Re-authentication needs the user-present case added without dropping the existing user-absent conditional-UI setup.
